# Captions and table notes (figtab-repo -> paper-repo); one entry per delivered item

## Table 1 (appendix; tables/table1_audit.tex), generated by figures/scripts/table1_audit.py from experiment-repo results/audit.csv
Title: Data audit of the 13 binary score matrices after de-duplication.
Note: Rows are the file names of the data repository (commit 55faff49). Models: rows kept after dropping repeated model names and rows identical to an earlier row ("Dup. dropped" counts both). Families: distinct model families derived from the names by keyword (heuristic); for LegalBench the row-to-model mapping is not published, so families are unknown and every row counts as its own. Constant items: items answered identically by all models (kept). Full score: min / median / max of the models' full-benchmark accuracy. All matrices were checked to be binary.

## Fig. 1 (main text; figures/fig1_protocol.pdf), figures/scripts/fig1_protocol.py (no data)
Caption: The protocol. A design picks n items using only the source models' results; the target model is run on those n items only; an estimator turns its n answers (and the source matrix) into a predicted full-benchmark score, which is compared with the true score. The three splits differ in which models play the target.

## Table 2 (main text; tables/table2_primary.tex), figures/scripts/tables234.py from results/primary.csv and results/selected.csv
Title: Primary endpoint: RMSE of the predicted full score relative to uniform random sampling, n = 100 items.
Note: Entry = geometric mean over benchmarks of RMSE / RMSE of uniform × mean on the same targets and draws, [95% family-bootstrap interval; 2000 replicates, target families resampled within each benchmark]. Below 1 is better than uniform. Thin cells (< 10 targets or < 5 families) are excluded; the lineage split is defined for 12 benchmarks (LegalBench has no family information). Methods are design × estimator; the first seven rows are fixed class representatives (one per method class), the last three are the best methods by this endpoint and were chosen after seeing the results, so their intervals and ratios are optimistic. Third block: for each of five method classes, the cell chosen by leave-one-benchmark-out (the cell with the smallest geometric-mean ratio on the other benchmarks of the same split is applied to the held-out benchmark; the row is the geometric mean over held-out benchmarks), which does not use the outcomes of the benchmark it is scored on. Last block: same quantity against stratified × mean as the baseline. The bottom rows count benchmarks, targets and target families, summed over the benchmarks entering. Benchmarks are not independent (HELM models recur across its benchmarks, OLL families across OLL benchmarks); the interval reflects target-family sampling only.

```console
So the sources buy about a fifth of the error of a stratified sample when targets resemble them, and in extrapolation at most a tenth, which a balanced design with calibrated regression already delivers.
The gain comes mostly from the seven Open LLM Leaderboard benchmarks (balanced $\times$ difference IRT $0.71$ and $0.75$ of stratified sampling in interpolation and lineage); on the six HELM benchmarks, with about $80$ overlapping models each, it is $0.92$ and $1.00$ and the IRT model alone is no better than uniform ($0.95$ in interpolation; Table~\ref{tab:suite}).
With the top 10\% of models as targets the best difference cell reaches $0.70$ $[0.68,0.72]$ of uniform's error, with the top 50\% $0.96$ $[0.92,0.98]$, and uniform $\times$ difference IRT is barely below uniform ($0.97$ $[0.95,0.99]$).
At a budget of $2\%$ of each benchmark's items (between $9$ and $241$ items; Table~\ref{tab:twopct}) the pattern is the same and the sources buy more: the best difference cell is $0.69$ $[0.67,0.70]$ of stratified sampling in interpolation and $0.87$ $[0.85,0.89]$ in extrapolation, and the IRT model alone is $1.36$ times uniform in extrapolation.
With few source models the gain disappears (Figure~\ref{fig:msrc}): at $10$ sources balanced $\times$ difference IRT is $1.10$ and $1.04$ of uniform in interpolation and extrapolation, at $30$ it is $0.80$ and $0.86$, while stratified sampling, which needs the sources only to order items, hardly changes ($0.85$ to $0.81$ in interpolation).

\subsection{Where does the bias of model-based predictors sit?}
```

```console
#5 Version 1: paper, code and figure scripts (recalibrated estimator not yet run)
State:   open

Changes: +15004 -2 (94 files)

First version: the delivered paper as it stands on `dev`. It holds the abstract, introduction, results from the full runs (13 benchmarks, three splits, two sensitivity splits, the 2% endpoint, the source-count runs and the leave-one-benchmark-out representatives), the discussion and limitations, the appendices, the filled checklist, the code package, and the scripts of every figure and table. The target-recalibrated estimator and two-phase design asked for in the Brief, and a nested split with a larger gap above the sources, are not yet run; the paper states none of them as run, and the extrapolation conclusions will be revised when they are.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
### Review

Review is Forgejo's pull request review: approve, or request changes and say what must change; a comment neither approves nor holds anything. A pull request into `main` of `paper-repo` waits for the owners of the paths it changes, and one into its `release` or `final` waits for the approval of `internal-review-repo`, the only one counted there, of the very commit it merges: a push to it after the approval withdraws it. A review request stands until its reviewer reviews, and a review until its reviewer reviews again: nobody withdraws or dismisses another's.

### Versions and release

A version for the world's users is a merge of `main` into `release` of `paper-repo`, by a pull request that `internal-review-repo` approved and whose checks pass. The system writes the checks as commit statuses on the pull request's head (`hutian/delivery`, and the world's contract's when it holds one), and a failing one says what is missing and who provides it; nobody else writes a status. Merge with a merge commit, not a squash or a rebase, or the next version conflicts. The system publishes each version as a release of `world/result`, the world's results, with the delivery attached: the users of the world read those releases and nothing else, and every role reads them. The last approval is a merge into `final` in the same way: the system releases the world from it, at once, and nothing pushed after it is part of it. Offer a `release` version as soon as the delivery holds its main work, so that `internal-review-repo`'s review comes while there is still room to act on it; `final` is the last. Do not ask another role to review the same unchanged delivery twice merely to pass through both branches. A release goes to the world's user; no role submits it to a venue or declares a licence for it.

When the world is quiet, the system hands each remaining gap of the delivery to its owner once, and once more when `main` of `paper-repo` has moved since; if it goes quiet again before a gap, a version, an open request or a review changes, the world ends there, unless a tracked job is still running, or the world runs to a wall-clock limit with someone outside attending it and all that is left is that `paper-repo` has proposed no version, with nothing failed and nothing open but requests that `ht-human` opened and their owners have seen: then it waits instead of ending, up to that limit. So whatever needs another role's action must be open where that role owns it.
```

shown.message:
`paper-repo` `dev` and the open pull request `paper-repo`#5 into `main` now carry the 13-benchmark redraw, and I'm waiting for the owners to review it again.

- **Figures and tables:** I copied `figures/` and `tables/` from `figtab-repo` 18bc23b into `dev`. That includes the new robustness table, which the text cites as `tab:robust`. The system build of `dev` now has no undefined references.
- **Text changes:**
  - **2% budget:** the text now reports the leave-one-benchmark-out classes against stratified sampling. They are 0.63–0.73 in interpolation. In extrapolation they are 0.88–0.93 for the info-top/CAT, design-based and difference-corrected classes, 0.96 for anchors and 0.99 for the model-based class.
  - **Anchor wording:** the intro, abstract and results now say anchor selection is "not clearly better than uniform sampling". The intro gives the intervals, 0.95 [0.89, 1.00] and 1.03 [0.93, 1.09].
- **Page budget:** the build is 25 pages, the main text ends on page 9, and the references start on page 10.
- **Pull request #5:**
  - **Branch:** I pushed `dev` to `candidate-first`.
  - **Comment:** my comment on #5 answers `experiment-repo`'s three items.
  - **Review state:** that review still stands as rejected until `experiment-repo` reviews again.
  - **Title:** it still says "recalibrated estimator not yet run", which stays true.
- **Request #6:** closed.

Still outstanding: the recalibrated-estimator and 100-draw results from `experiment-repo`. Once they land I'll add the recalibrated result and re-check the abstract and the page count. After the owners approve #5 into `main`, I'll offer `main` to `release`.
